title: plot_seasonal
text:
plot_seasonal() is TSForge’s diagnostic visualization engine — designed to reveal the underlying shape, stability, and distribution of seasonal patterns.
While standard line plots show what happened, seasonal plots explain when it happens. This function is critical for answering: - Is there a pattern? (Do sales always spike in Q4?) - Is the pattern stable? (Did the Q4 spike stop happening in 2023?) - Are there anomalies? (Was that March drop normal seasonality or a supply shock?)
It supports: - Trend Normalization: Compare seasonal shapes even when sales double year-over-year. - Signal Extraction: Visualize the “True Average Seasonality” overlaid on noisy data. - Boxplot & Line Modes: Switch between distributional views and trajectory views. - Interactive Modes: Overlay, Facet, and Dropdown layouts.

title: plot_seasonal
text:
Analysis Controls








Parameter
Type
Description




freq
str
The seasonal cycle to plot. Options: "M" (Month), "Q" (Quarter), "W" (Week), "D" (Day).


normalize
bool
Critical. If True, divides each year’s data by that year’s mean. Removes trend to isolate seasonal shape.


show_mean
bool
If True (and kind="line"), overlays the average seasonal pattern as a bold dashed line.


seasonal_agg
str
Aggregation function used when collapsing data (default: "mean").

title: plot_seasonal
text:
Rendering & Styling








Parameter
Type
Description




kind
str
"line" (yearly trajectories) or "box" (distributions).


mode
str
"overlay" (all on one), "facet" (small multiples), or "dropdown" (interactive).


engine
str
"plotly" (interactive, default) or "matplotlib" (static).


ids
list
Specific ID(s) to filter. If None, samples up to 6 random IDs.

title: tsforge
text:
tsforge is a Python package for building and managing forecasting features.
It’s designed to make it easy to:

🏗️ Engineer time series features (lags, rolling stats, seasonalities)

⚡ Scale feature creation across many series quickly

🔗 Integrate cleanly with Nixtla’s ecosystem (statsforecast, mlforecast, etc.)

📈 Support end-to-end forecasting pipelines





Getting Started

Feature Engineering






Forecasting is rarely just “fit a model.” Most of the heavy lifting happens in data prep and feature engineering.
tsforge gives you a reliable, repeatable toolkit for that messy step, so you can spend more time on modeling and decision-making.




```bash pip install tsforge

title: plot_timeseries
text:
plot_timeseries() is TSForge’s flagship visualization engine — a modular, enterprise-grade Plotly interface that supports:

Overlay, facet, and dropdown views

Hierarchical time series

Global & local events

Anomalies

Forecasts + prediction intervals

Multiple professional themes

Smoothing

Auto-selection of IDs when a dataset is large

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Event Styling


Code
events_config = {
  "color": "#444",
  "opacity": 0.85,
  "stagger_labels": True
}

plot_timeseries(
  df_actuals,
  id_col="unique_id",
  date_col="ds",
  value_col="y",
  events_global=events_global,
  events_config=events_config,
)

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Anomaly Styling


Code
plot_timeseries(
  df_actuals,
  id_col="unique_id",
  date_col="ds",
  value_col="y",
  anomalies=anoms_df,
  anomalies_config={
    "color": "crimson",
    "marker_symbol": "x",
    "marker_size": 10
  }
)

title: plot_timeseries
text:
Theme Styling


Code
fig = plot_timeseries(
    df=df_actuals,
    id_col="unique_id",
    date_col="ds",
    value_col="y",
    events_global=events_global,
    anomalies=anoms_df,
    mode="overlay",
    theme="dark",
)
fig

Parameter
Description

Forecast DataFrame containing yhat and prediction interval columns.

List of uncertainty interval levels (e.g., [80, 95]).


lo_pattern
Pattern for lower PI column names.


hi_pattern
